summary: Dekese is a remote, forested territory in northern Kasaï along the Lukenie river, bordering Sankuru and Mai-Ndombe. It was not a significant theatre of the 2016-2017 Kamuina Nsapu insurgency and no armed group is known to hold territory there as of 2026. Dekese town is administered by the state with a PNC commissariat; villages rely on PNC posts and customary chiefs. Live web research was unavailable in this run, so assessments rest on background knowledge and default state presence.
